newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shell says considering refining partner in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Shell says considering refining partner in Europe.

text.p: Royal Dutch/Shell said on Thursday it was considering teaming up with another oil major in Europe in an effort to lift sagging refining margins.

"Both we and the industry have much to do. We continue in discussions with a number of potential partners. You will continue to see changes," group director Steve Miller told a news conference in the Hague.
He did not reveal the names of the potential partners.
He added that the company's recent announcements that it would reduce European refining capacity were not necessarily the last it would make.

In December, Shell said it planned to sell its 60,000 bpd Cressier refinery in Switzerland and, in the last week, said it would scale down capacity at its 128,000 bpd Berre refinery in the south of France.
Co-chairman John Jennings, speaking in London, agreed that the industry required more capacity cuts.
"I think it's one step and it doesn't solve the problem," he said.

Shell Netherlands president Jan Slechte reinforced the view that margins remain unhealthy by saying that the company's single refinery in the Netherlands, at Pernis, was only able to make a profit in 1996 with gains from oil stock revaluation.
"The refinery operation result was negative. We had some stock profits and overall made a very modest profit," he said.
Despite the gloom, group refining margins improved in 1996.
"Compared with 1995, the margins were slightly better, but they are not yet at a level where we can get much success," said group director Maarten van den Bergh.
The group's fourth quarter earnings excluding special items from refining and marketing were five percent down year on year, largely because the marketing side suffered.
"Rising supply costs and competitive pressures, mainly in Europe and particularly in the UK, resulted in lower marketing earnings than in the previous year," the company said in a statement.
